headline: Record revenue drives EPS growth as margins widen
summary_short: FNB's Q2 2026 diluted EPS of $0.42 rose 16.7% y/y and 10.5% q/q on record revenue of $462.7M and net income of $148.7M, with pre-provision net revenue up 8.8% q/q and CET1 holding at 11.4%.
summary_long: Net interest income rose to $365.7M (+5.3% y/y, +1.8% q/q) as earning-asset growth and lower funding costs offset a lower loan yield; NIM (FTE) rose 6bp y/y to 3.25%, flat q/q. Non-interest income grew 6.5% y/y to $97.0M on wealth-management and capital-markets fees. Expenses rose 2.9% y/y but fell 1.8% q/q as seasonal comp costs receded, pushing the efficiency ratio to 53.7% from 56.1% q/q. Credit quality stayed solid: provision $21.4M, NPLs 0.31% of loans. Deposits were $38.7B, loans $35.8B, CET1 held at 11.4%, and the company repurchased $47M of stock.

drivers.explanation: EPS growth outpaced net income growth because diluted shares outstanding fell 1.3% y/y and 0.8% q/q on the quarter's $47M buyback, per the release's capital-actions and share-count disclosures.

Net interest income rose 5.3% y/y on earning-asset growth and lower funding costs, and non-interest income rose 6.5% y/y on wealth-management and capital-markets fees, partially offset by 2.9% y/y higher expense from merit increases and technology investment.
Same revenue and expense drivers as net income; the effective tax rate also fell to 20.9% from 21.5% y/y, per the release, widening the after-tax increase relative to pre-tax.
Cash funded loan growth of $653M q/q alongside a $524M q/q increase in short-term borrowings, per the balance sheet; the release does not state a direct cause for the cash decline.
Loan growth exceeded deposit growth at quarter end, lifting the loan-to-deposit ratio to 92.5% from 90.3% q/q, per the release; higher wholesale short-term borrowings funded the gap.

Equity grew on retained-earnings accumulation from net income less dividends, partially offset by a wider accumulated-other-comprehensive-loss and higher treasury stock from the $47M buyback, per the balance sheet detail.
Diluted share count fell as the company repurchased $47 million, or 2.7 million shares, of common stock during the quarter, per the release's capital-actions disclosure.

CEO cited record revenue, 17% y/y EPS growth, positive operating leverage, 9% y/y pre-provision net revenue growth, and 7% annualized linked-quarter loan growth while maintaining credit discipline; no numeric forward guidance range was given.
